subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's internal yielding walker and bootstrap-hook interleaving changes as the scoped fix for the bootstrap-context event-loop stall before broader Gateway worker/offload work?
rationale: The patch appears technically correct, but it changes compatibility-sensitive internal scheduling and traversal semantics used during plugin hook execution and embedded agent bootstrap preparation.

options.title: Accept the scoped mitigation
options.body: Merge after maintainer review, treating the traversal and hook interleaving changes as acceptable internal behavior for protecting Gateway availability.

options.title: Require connected runtime proof
options.body: Ask for a full embedded_run/channel proof showing keepalives or cheap Gateway work proceeding during bootstrap before accepting the scheduling change.

options.title: Defer to broader architecture work
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, caching, or priority scheduling to own this class of stalls instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped mitigation
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainer review, treating the traversal and hook interleaving changes as acceptable internal behavior for protecting Gateway availability.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest history match for the bootstrap read and internal hook/bootstrap architecture paths affected by the decision.
